flat.breakdown_boundary: Breaks at dimensionality: WES is finite point sets in R^2; martensitic is infinite periodic lattice in R^3.

flat.physics_desc: Diffusionless solid-state phase transition: BCC->FCC/BCT via Bain correspondence. sqrt(2) contraction along one axis, sqrt(2) expansion transversely. Square geometry is metastable (zero off-axis slack); hexagonal geometry stable. Mechanism: coord-4 lattice has no slack under shear. Same geometric mechanism as square-packing brittleness in math.
flat.physics_invariant: BCC is the extremizer: any shear finds Bain path to FCC; zero slack in square geometry
flat.transfer_operator: sqrt(2) brittleness: both systems at saddle in config space; orthogonal geometry is the unique critical point

flat.breakdown_boundary: Breaks at continuous vs discrete: Chebyshev is continuous polynomials; phase transition is discrete lattice.
flat.math_invariant: Chebyshev minimizes L-inf norm; sqrt(2) ratio governs extremizer in coefficient space
flat.physics_desc: Body-centered cubic (coord-8) to face-centered cubic (coord-12) transition under pressure/temperature. BCC sqrt(2)-neighbor geometry is brittle under shear; FCC/HCP hexagonal-close-packed geometry is robust. The sqrt(2)/sqrt(3) ratio distinguishes brittle from stable lattice geometry. Bain path is the minimal-energy transformation path.
flat.physics_invariant: Bain path passes through BCT saddle at c/a = sqrt(2); minimum-energy transformation path
flat.transfer_operator: Geometric extremizers share same constraint: orthogonal symmetry forces saddle rather than minimum

flat.breakdown_boundary: Breaks at 3D vs 1D: Roche lobe is 3D equipotential with rotation; sublevel set is 1D Lebesgue measure. Rotational kinetic energy term in Roche potential has no polynomial analog. Eggleton predicts alpha_opt~0.30; actual is ~0.17.
flat.math_invariant: Extremal measure = atom(0.828) at +1 plus discrete cloud(0.172) near -1; inf <= 1.8373; optimal alpha ~0.172

flat.physics_desc: Two-body gravitational problem: elliptical orbits. T^2 proportional to a^3. Conserved Runge-Lenz vector gives closed orbits.
flat.physics_invariant: Minimum Roche lobe at mass ratio q via Eggleton (1983); L1 Lagrange point at barycentre; qualitatively predicts binary structure but quantitatively wrong: Eggleton minimizes at alpha~0.30 not 0.17
flat.physics_object: Roche lobe volume minimization in binary star system
flat.transfer_operator: ln|x-t| potential <-> gravitational potential; sublevel set <-> Roche lobe; x=0 boundary <-> L1 Lagrange point. Qualitative: correctly identifies binary endpoint concentration. Quantitative: Eggleton 3D formula overestimates optimal alpha by ~75% due to rotational terms absent in 1D polynomial problem.
